overrides.text: Burek: there is no USDA burek, so the values are from a Croatian producer’s cheese burek (Čakovečki mlinovi: 297 kcal, 16 g fat, 3.3 g sugar per 100 g). overrides.source: Čakovečki mlinovi, Burek (net weight 150 g; “slojevi tijesta i sirnog nadjeva”, layers of dough and cheese filling): energy 1241 kJ / 297 kcal, fat 16 g, saturates 7.5 g, carbohydrate 29 g, sugars 3.3 g, protein 9.7 g, salt 1.4 g. Basis: Regulation (EU) 1169/2011 Art. 32(2) “shall be expressed per 100 g or per 100 ml”. Range: Sofka beef burek 247 kcal, Lidl meat burek 316 kcal (Open Food Facts 9120018535583, 4056489610953)
overrides.note: Sodium = 1.4 / 2.5 = 560 mg. Fiber not declared (None). Water stays from the USDA turnover proxy. Basis checked 2026-10-19 on the producer's web page (EN and HR), not on the pack: the table has no column header; per 100 g follows from EU 1169/2011 Art. 32(2), from Atwater (16×9 + 29×4 + 9.7×4 = 299 kcal ≈ 297, i.e. 54.7 g of macros per 100 g, plausible for burek), from the same page's 400 g breads at 222 and 260 kcal (per 100 g), and from other burek labels (247-316 kcal/100 g); per piece it would be 198 kcal/100 g, below every label. Level B until read on the pack.

src.text: Chicken: 150 g of meat (roasted chicken thigh with skin, USDA). Twenty döner kebabs bought and weighed in Italy averaged 402 g with 35–40% meat, about 150 g; a German TV test weighed 80–173 g of meat; USDA’s gyro uses 60 g. The study found skin in the döner meat and 8.6 g of fat per 100 g of kebab, which skinless thigh meat cannot reach, so we use thigh with skin.

src.text: Beef/veal: 150 g of meat; the closest USDA record is grilled ground beef 80/20 (German rules allow up to 60% minced meat in a döner). Weighed döner kebabs in Italy carried about 150 g of meat (35–40% of a 402 g kebab); measured portions run from 60 g (USDA gyro) to about 230 g.

src.text: Mayonnaise sauce: 14 g (USDA guideline amount on a regular sandwich). The Italian study reports that kebab shops mostly used supermarket mayonnaise and ketchup; without it the kebab has about a third less fat than the study measured.

src.text: Kebab is our builder: pita or wrap, chicken or beef, vegetables and sauce, each a USDA record. The amounts follow twenty döner kebabs bought and weighed in Italian shops (402 g: 37% meat, 25% bread, 25% vegetables, 13% sauce). Our default has about the study’s measured fat and protein per 100 g. The study’s 226 kcal per 100 g is gross energy from burning the food in a calorimeter; the energy the body can use from its measured protein, fat and starch is about 177–187 kcal per 100 g, and ours is 192. Kebab shops differ a lot, mostly in the meat.
src.cite: Panozzo et al. 2015, Ital J Food Saf 4:4535 (20 weighed döner kebabs); RTL test via Mallorca Revue; USDA FNDDS 2706962 gyro
